newsitem.title: USA: Alcoa earnings drop in fourth quarter.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa earnings drop in fourth quarter.

text.p: Aluminum Co. of America Wednesday reported surprisingly weak fourth-quarter earnings as aluminum prices fell and raw materials costs rose.
The decline was partly offset by higher alumina prices, the company's improved performance and stronger sales of non-aluminum products.

Alcoa's profits slipped to $136.1 million, or 78 cents a share, in the fourth quarter, from $150.9 million, or 85 cents a share, in the year-ago period. The earnings per share were far lower than the Wall Street consensus estimate of 86 cents.
Revenues edged up to $3.29 billion from $3.14 billion.

The results include an after-tax charge of $16.8 million, or 10 cents per share, for impairments, as well as after-tax gains of $8 million, or 5 cents per share, from valuing certain aluminum commodity contracts at market prices instead of contract prices, Alcoa said.
Aided by Alcoa's acquired operations in Italy, Alcoa said shipments of aluminum products during the fourth quarter rose to 747,000 metric tons from 646,000 tons in the year-ago period.
Alcoa's stock edged down 12.5 cents to $67.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
